# Trellix Source




The Trellix Source receives structured detection data from [Trellix Network Detection and Response (NDR)](https://docs.trellix.com/bundle/ndr_4.x_console_pg/page/UUID-fbd79d07-0ff2-7d62-a8bf-5c47c01b3ad3.html) using the HTTP Event Collector (HEC) protocol. This Source supports the `/services/collector/event` endpoint. It doesn't support the `/services/collector/raw` endpoint or HEC indexer acknowledgements.

> Type: **Push**  |  TLS Support: **Yes**  |  Event Breaker Support: **No**
>
> This Source supports gzip-compressed inbound data when the `Content-Encoding: gzip` connection header is set.
>


## Configure a Trellix Source

1. On the top bar, select **Products**, and then select **Cribl Stream**. Under **Worker Groups**, select a Worker Group. Next, you have two options:
   - To configure via [QuickConnect](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/quickconnect), navigate to **Routing** > **QuickConnect**. Select **Add Source** and select the Source you want from the list, choosing either **Select Existing** or **Add New**.
   - To configure via the [Routes](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/routes), select **Data** > **Sources**. Select **Add Source**, and then select **Trellix**.
1. In the **New Source** modal, configure the following under **General Settings**:
   - **Input ID**: Enter a unique name to identify this Source definition. If you clone this Source, Cribl Stream adds `-CLONE` to the original **Input ID**.
   - **Description**: Enter a description for this Source.
   - **Address**: Enter the hostname or IP address on which to listen for HTTP or HTTPS data. Defaults to `0.0.0.0`. Supports IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
   - **Port**: Enter the port number on which to listen.
   - **HEC endpoint**: Keep the default `/services/collector`. Cribl Stream derives the event and health endpoints from this base path. See [Send Data to the HEC Endpoints](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#endpoints).
1. Under **Optional Settings**, configure the following:
   - **Allowed indexes**: Enter values to allow in the HEC event `index` field. Supports wildcards. Leave blank to skip validation. These values can expand index validation at the token level.
   - **Tags**: Add tags that you can use to filter and group Sources. These tags aren't added to processed events.
1. Optionally, adjust the [TLS](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#tls), [persistent queue](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#pq), [Processing](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#processing), [Auth Tokens](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#auth-tokens), and [Advanced](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#advanced) settings, or [Connected Destinations](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#connected).
1. Select **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

### TLS Settings (Server Side)

**Enabled**: Toggle on to enable Transport Layer Security (TLS) on this connection. Defaults to toggled off. When toggled on, configure the following settings.

Under **Server Certificate**, select a certificate from the store to auto-fill the paths, or enter them manually:

- **Certificate**: Select an existing certificate name from the drop-down or add a new certificate by selecting **Create**. See [Add a TLS Certificate to a Worker Group](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/securing-sources-dest#add-certificate-to-group) for details.
- **Certificate path**: Enter the server path that contains certificates in Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) format. You can reference `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Private key path**: Enter the server path that contains the private key in PEM format. You can reference `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Passphrase**: Enter the passphrase used to decrypt the private key.

Under **Mutual Authentication (mTLS)**:

- **Authenticate client (mutual auth)**: Toggle on to require clients to present certificates. Defaults to toggled off. When toggled on, configure these settings:
  - **Trusted client CA path**: Enter the server path that contains the certificate authority (CA) certificates to trust as the chain root when verifying a client's identity.
  - **Validate client certificates**: Toggle on to reject certificates that aren't authorized by a CA in the **Trusted client CA path** or by another trusted CA. Defaults to toggled on.
  - **Common name**: Enter a regex to match against the CN and SAN fields in the client certificate. Cribl Stream rejects clients unless it finds at least one match. Defaults to `/.*/`.

Under **TLS Version**, reject clients using TLS versions below or above these thresholds:

- **Minimum TLS version**: Select the minimum TLS version to accept.
- **Maximum TLS version**: Select the maximum TLS version to accept.

### Persistent Queue Settings

In the **Persistent Queue Settings** tab, you can optionally specify persistent queue storage, using the following controls. Persistent queue buffers and preserves incoming events when a downstream Destination has an outage or experiences backpressure.

Before enabling persistent queue, learn more about persistent queue behavior and how to optimize it with your system:

- [About Persistent Queues](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues)
- [Optimize Source Persistent Queues](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues-sources)

> On Cribl-managed [Cloud](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/deploy-cloud) Workers (with an [Enterprise plan](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/cloud-enterprise)), this tab exposes only the **Enable persistent queue** toggle. If enabled, PQ is automatically configured in `Always On` mode, with a maximum queue size of 1 GB disk space allocated per PQ-enabled Source, per Worker Process.
>
> The 1 GB limit is on uncompressed inbound data, and the queue does not perform any compression. This limit is not configurable. For configurable queue size, compression, mode, and other options below, use a [hybrid Group](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/cloud-enterprise#hybrid).
>
> All other settings described in this section apply to on-prem and hybrid deployments only.
>


**Enable persistent queue**: Default is toggled off. When toggled on:

**Mode**: Select a condition for engaging persistent queues.

- `Always On`: This default option will always write events to the persistent queue, before forwarding them to the Cribl Stream data processing engine.
- `Smart`: This option will engage PQ only when the Source detects backpressure from the Cribl Stream data processing engine. `Smart` mode only engages when necessary, such as when a downstream Destination becomes blocked *and* the **Buffer size limit** reaches its limit. When persistent queue is set to `Smart` mode, Cribl Stream attempts to flush the queue when every new event arrives. The only time events stay in the buffer is when a downstream Destination becomes blocked.

> **Deprecation Notice**
>
> To improve data integrity, **Smart** mode is deprecated for Source persistent queue on hybrid and on-prem deployments. In January 2027, affected configurations will automatically migrate to **Always On** mode. Consider updating existing configurations to **Always On** mode prior to the automatic migration date. Before changing the configuration:
>
> - [Monitor](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues-sources#monitoring) your persistent queue usage so that you can [allocate enough disk space](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues-sources#queue-disk-space).
> - Before making changes to your persistent queue, remember to [drain the queues](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues#clear-pq) first to avoid orphaned data.
> - Verify that [data routing and filtering](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/routes) behaves as expected in a test environment before rolling out the new configuration to production.
>


**Buffer size limit (bytes)**: The maximum memory to buffer events before flushing them to persistent queue on disk. Enter a value with a unit suffix. For example: `64KB`, `1MB`, or `10MB`. Spaces between the number and unit are allowed (such as `64 KB`). Units are case-insensitive. Plain byte values (like `65536`) are accepted, but decimals (like `0.5MB`) are not. The valid range is `64KB` to `10MB`. Values outside this range are rounded to the nearest limit. Defaults to `1MB`.

> **Deprecation Notice**
>
>The **Buffer size limit (bytes)** setting replaces the deprecated **Buffer size limit (events)** setting as of version 4.18.0 to provide more predictable memory management. For upgraded Worker Groups and Fleets, the new byte-based limit defaults to `1MB`. Update your configurations to use the byte-based limit to ensure optimal memory stability.
>


**Commit frequency**: The number of events to send downstream before committing that Cribl Stream has read them. Defaults to `42`.

**File size limit**: The maximum data volume to store in each queue file before closing it and (optionally) applying the configured **Compression**. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, and so on. If not specified, Cribl Stream applies the default `10 MB`. When you save the configuration, **File size limit** must be greater than or equal to **Buffer size limit (bytes)**. Cribl Stream rejects invalid combinations.

**Queue size limit**: The maximum amount of disk space that the queue is allowed to consume on each Worker Process. Once this limit is reached, this Source stops queueing data and applies the **Queue-full behavior**. Required, and defaults to `5` GB. Accepts positive numbers with units of `KB`, `MB`, `GB`, and so on. Can be set as high as `1 TB`, unless you've [configured](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/group-settings#storage) a different **Worker Process PQ size limit** in Group or Fleet settings.

**Queue file path**: The location for the persistent queue files. Defaults to `$CRIBL_HOME/state/queues`. To this field's specified path, Cribl Stream appends `/<worker-id>/inputs/<input-id>`.

**Compression**: Optional codec to compress the persisted data after a file closes. Defaults to `None`; `Gzip` is also available.

**Queue-full behavior**: Whether to block or drop events when the queue begins to exert backpressure. A queue begins to exert backpressure when the disk is low or at full capacity.

  - **Block** (Default): Does not accept new data until the queue has capacity. When the sender supports backpressure signaling, Cribl Stream returns block signals to the sender.
  - **Drop new data**: Discards incoming events while leaving the contents of the persistent queue unchanged.

> In Cribl Stream 4.1 and newer, the Source persistent queue default **Mode** is `Always on`, to best ensure events' delivery. For details on optimizing this selection, see [Optimize Source Persistent Queues](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/persistent-queues-sources).
>
> You can optimize Workers' startup connections and CPU load at **Group/Fleet settings** > [Worker Processes](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/group-settings#processes).
>


### Processing Settings

#### Fields

Select **Add Field** to add fields to each event using [Eval](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/eval-function)-like functionality:

- **Field Name**: Enter the field name.
- **Value**: Enter a JavaScript expression that determines the field's value.

Fields configured here can be overridden by fields added at the token or request level.

#### Pre-Processing

From the **Pipeline** list, select one [Pipeline](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/pipelines) or [Pack](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/packs) to process data before sending it through Routes.

### Auth Tokens

Add one or more tokens that Trellix NDR can use to authenticate. If you don't configure a token, the Source permits unauthorized access.

Select **Add Token**, and then configure the following for each token:

**Authentication method**: Select **Secret** to use a text secret. This Source doesn't support manually entered tokens.

**Token secret (text secret)**: Choose **Select local secret** or **Select global secret**, then select an existing text secret or select **Create text secret**.

**Enable token**: Toggle on to allow client access with this token. Defaults to toggled on.

**Description**: Enter a description for the token. The description becomes the token's display name.

**Allowed indexes**: Enter values to allow in the HEC event `index` field at the token level. Supports wildcards. Leave blank to skip validation.

**Fields**: Select **Add Field** to add fields to events that reference this token. Each field is a **Field Name** and **Value** pair.

### Advanced Settings

**Emit per-token request metrics**: Toggle on to emit per-token `<prefix>.http.perToken` and summary `<prefix>.http.summary` request metrics. Defaults to toggled off.

**Show originating IP**: Toggle on to extract the client IP address and port from PROXY protocol v1 or v2. When toggled on, Cribl Stream ignores the `X-Forwarded-For` header. Defaults to toggled off.

**Capture request headers**: Toggle on to add request headers to events in the `__headers` field. Defaults to toggled off.

> When **Capture request headers** is enabled, this Source stores request headers in the `__headers` field. Some Destinations also read `__headers` for outbound behavior. HTTP Destinations such as [Webhook](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-webhook), [Loki](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-loki), [Microsoft Sentinel](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-sentinel), [Dynatrace HTTP](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-dynatrace-http), and [Cortex XSIAM](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-xsiam) use it to inject dynamic request headers. [Kafka](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-kafka) Destinations use it for message headers. Other Destinations that read `__headers` can be affected the same way. Forwarding captured events to these Destinations without removing `__headers` can cause TLS validation failures or expose inbound authentication headers. Use an [Eval](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/eval-function) Function in a Pipeline to remove `__headers` (or copy it to another field name, then remove `__headers`) before the Destination. See [`__headers` field conflicts](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#headers-conflict).



**CORS allowed origins**: Enter HTTP origins to which Cribl Stream sends Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers. Supports wildcards.

**CORS allowed headers**: Enter HTTP headers that Cribl Stream sends to allowed origins as `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` in a CORS preflight response. Enter `*` to allow all headers.

**Active request limit**: Enter the maximum number of active requests allowed per Worker Process. Defaults to `256`. Enter `0` for unlimited. This setting is available only for on-prem deployments.

**Activity log sample rate**: Enter how often Cribl Stream logs request activity at the `info` level. Defaults to `100`, which logs every 100th request. The minimum value is `1`.

**Requests-per-socket limit**: Enter the maximum number of requests allowed per socket before Cribl Stream instructs the client to close the connection. Defaults to `0`, which allows unlimited requests.

**Socket timeout (seconds)**: Enter how long Cribl Stream waits before treating an inactive socket as timed out. Defaults to `0`, which waits indefinitely.

**Request timeout (seconds)**: Enter how long Cribl Stream waits for an incoming request to complete before aborting it. Defaults to `0`, which disables the timeout.

**Keep-alive timeout (seconds)**: Enter how long Cribl Stream waits for more data after sending the last response. Defaults to `5` seconds. The minimum is `1` second, and the maximum is `600` seconds.

**IP allowlist regex**: Enter a regex that matches IP addresses whose messages Cribl Stream processes, unless the denylist also matches. Defaults to `/.*/`.

**IP denylist regex**: Enter a regex that matches IP addresses whose messages Cribl Stream ignores. The denylist takes precedence over the allowlist. Defaults to `/^$/`.

**Environment**: If you're using GitOps, enter the Git branch on which to enable this configuration. Leave blank to enable the configuration everywhere.

### Connected Destinations

Select **Send to Routes** to enable conditional routing, filtering, and cloning of this Source's data via the Routing table.

Select **QuickConnect** to send this Source's data to one or more Destinations via independent, direct connections.

## Configure Trellix NDR to Forward Data

After you save this Source, add a Splunk integration in Trellix NDR. See Trellix's [Configure SIEM using Web UI](https://docs.trellix.com/bundle/ndr_4.x_console_pg/page/UUID-2103cb9d-568f-5d93-a2db-aca0f55d47cc.html) documentation.

Use these values for the Splunk integration:

- **IP address or hostname**: Enter the address that Trellix NDR uses to reach this Source.
- **Port**: Enter the **Port** of this Source.
- **Authentication**: Enter the value of a text secret you referenced under [Auth Tokens](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#auth-tokens).
- **SSL**: Enable SSL if you enabled TLS on this Source.
- **Notification**: Enable notifications to send alerts, Layer 7 metadata, and flow events to the Source.

## Send Data to the HEC Endpoints

Keep **HEC endpoint** set to `/services/collector`. Trellix NDR sends structured events to `/services/collector/event`. This Source also accepts health checks at `/services/collector/health`. These paths follow Splunk's [HEC REST API endpoints](https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-started/get-data-in/10.2/get-data-with-http-event-collector/http-event-collector-rest-api-endpoints).

Requests to `/services/collector/raw` return HTTP `404`. Requests to `/services/collector/ack` return HTTP `400` with the text `ACK is disabled`.

## Internal Fields

Cribl Stream uses internal fields to help process data from this Source:

- `__headers`: Contains request headers when **Capture request headers** is toggled on.
- `__hecToken`: Contains the HEC token associated with the event.
- `__inputId`: Identifies the Source in the format `trellix_hec:<input-id>`.
- `__srcIpPort`: Contains the source IP address and port.

## Troubleshooting

The Source's configuration modal has helpful tabs for troubleshooting:

**Live Data**: Try capturing [live data](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources#capture-source-data) to see real-time events as they are ingested. On the **Live Data** tab, click **Start Capture** to begin viewing real-time data.

**Logs**: Review and search the logs that provide detailed information about the ingestion process, including any errors or warnings that may have occurred.

You can also view the [Monitoring](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/monitoring) page that provides a comprehensive overview of data volume and rate, helping you identify ingestion issues. Analyze the graphs showing events and bytes in/out over time.

### `__headers` Field Conflicts with Destinations

When **Capture request headers** is enabled, this Source writes inbound headers to the `__headers` field. Some Destinations also use `__headers` for outbound HTTP headers or related TLS behavior, so the fields can interfere silently. Destinations that read `__headers` include HTTP Destinations such as [Webhook](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-webhook), [Loki](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-loki), [Microsoft Sentinel](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-sentinel), [Dynatrace HTTP](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-dynatrace-http), and [Cortex XSIAM](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-xsiam), which use it for dynamic request headers, and [Kafka](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-kafka) Destinations, which use it for message headers. Other Destinations that read `__headers` can be affected the same way.

In that case, events can leave Cribl Stream successfully (Source, Route, and Destination metrics look healthy) while data does not arrive or is rejected downstream. Destination logs may show no errors, or you may see TLS certificate or hostname validation failures, or authentication errors such as `invalid audience`.

To avoid the conflict, use an [Eval](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/eval-function) Function in a Pipeline to remove `__headers` before the Destination. To keep the captured headers under another name, add a field that copies `__headers`, then remove `__headers` (the [Rename](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/rename-function) Function cannot operate on fields whose names begin with `__`). If TLS or certificate errors appear and `__headers` contains a `host` value, you can also toggle **Validate server certs** off on the Destination. That weakens TLS verification, so use it only after you confirm the conflict is the cause.


### Requests Return `404` or `ACK is disabled`

See [Send Data to the HEC Endpoints](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/#endpoints).

# Configurar a Source Trellix

A Source Trellix recebe dados estruturados de detecção do Trellix Network Detection and Response (NDR) pelo protocolo HTTP Event Collector (HEC). Suporta o endpoint `/services/collector/event`. Não suporta `/services/collector/raw` nem confirmações do indexador HEC.

## Criar a Source no Cribl Stream

1. Na barra superior, selecione **Products** e **Cribl Stream**. Em **Worker Groups**, selecione o Worker Group.
   - Pelo QuickConnect: abra **Routing > QuickConnect**, selecione **Add Source** e escolha a Source, usando **Select Existing** ou **Add New**.
   - Pelas Routes: selecione **Data > Sources**, depois **Add Source** e **Trellix**.
2. No modal **New Source**, configure **General Settings**:
   - **Input ID**: nome exclusivo para identificar esta definição. Ao clonar a Source, o Cribl adiciona `-CLONE` ao Input ID original.
   - **Description**: descrição da Source.
   - **Address**: hostname ou endereço IP de escuta HTTP/HTTPS. O padrão é `0.0.0.0`; IPv4 e IPv6 são suportados.
   - **Port**: porta na qual a Source deve escutar.
   - **HEC endpoint**: mantenha `/services/collector`. O Cribl deriva desse caminho os endpoints de eventos e de saúde.
3. Em **Optional Settings**:
   - **Allowed indexes**: valores permitidos no campo HEC `index`. Aceita curingas; deixe vazio para não validar. Esses valores podem ampliar a validação de índices no nível de token.
   - **Tags**: tags para filtrar e agrupar Sources. Elas não são adicionadas aos eventos processados.
4. Ajuste, se necessário, **TLS**, **Persistent Queue**, **Processing**, **Auth Tokens**, **Advanced** e **Connected Destinations**. Consulte a página completa para todas as opções e restrições de implantação.
5. Selecione **Save** e **Commit & Deploy**.

## TLS no lado do servidor

**Enabled**: habilita TLS; o padrão é desabilitado. Se ativado, configure o certificado do servidor.

- **Certificate**: selecione um certificado existente ou use **Create** para adicionar outro.
- **Certificate path**: caminho dos certificados PEM no servidor; aceita `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Private key path**: caminho da chave privada PEM; aceita `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Passphrase**: senha para descriptografar a chave privada.

Para mTLS, habilite **Authenticate client (mutual auth)**, se necessário. Configure **Trusted client CA path** e **Validate client certificates**. Este último vem habilitado. Em **Common name**, defina a expressão regular para os campos CN e SAN do certificado do cliente; o padrão é `/.*/`.

Use **Minimum TLS version** e **Maximum TLS version** para limitar as versões aceitas.

## Auth Tokens

Adicione um ou mais tokens para autenticação do Trellix NDR. **Sem token configurado, a Source permite acesso sem autenticação.**

Selecione **Add Token** e configure:

- **Authentication method**: escolha **Secret**. Esta Source não suporta tokens inseridos manualmente.
- **Token secret (text secret)**: escolha **Select local secret** ou **Select global secret** e selecione um segredo de texto existente, ou use **Create text secret**.
- **Enable token**: permite acesso com esse token; vem habilitado.
- **Description**: descrição usada como nome de exibição do token.
- **Allowed indexes**: valores permitidos no campo HEC `index` para esse token; aceita curingas. Deixe vazio para não validar.
- **Fields**: use **Add Field** para adicionar pares **Field Name** e **Value** aos eventos que usam esse token.

## Configurar o Trellix NDR para encaminhar dados

Depois de salvar a Source, adicione uma integração Splunk no Trellix NDR, conforme [Configure SIEM using Web UI](https://docs.trellix.com/bundle/ndr_4.x_console_pg/page/UUID-2103cb9d-568f-5d93-a2db-aca0f55d47cc.html).

- **IP address or hostname**: endereço pelo qual o Trellix NDR alcança esta Source.
- **Port**: a porta configurada nesta Source.
- **Authentication**: valor do segredo de texto referenciado em **Auth Tokens**.
- **SSL**: habilite se TLS estiver habilitado na Source.
- **Notification**: habilite para enviar alertas, metadados de camada 7 e eventos de fluxo.

## Endpoints HEC

Mantenha **HEC endpoint** como `/services/collector`. O Trellix NDR envia eventos estruturados para `/services/collector/event`. A Source aceita verificações de saúde em `/services/collector/health`.

Requisições a `/services/collector/raw` retornam HTTP `404`. Requisições a `/services/collector/ack` retornam HTTP `400` com `ACK is disabled`.

Esta é a tradução revisada das seções de configuração. As opções detalhadas de persistent queues, processamento, configurações avançadas e troubleshooting estão na [página oficial completa](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/).

# Configurar el Source Trellix

El Source Trellix recibe datos estructurados de detección de Trellix Network Detection and Response (NDR) mediante HTTP Event Collector (HEC). Admite `/services/collector/event`. No admite `/services/collector/raw` ni confirmaciones del indexador HEC.

## Crear el Source en Cribl Stream

1. En la barra superior, seleccione **Products** y **Cribl Stream**. En **Worker Groups**, seleccione el Worker Group.
   - Mediante QuickConnect: abra **Routing > QuickConnect**, seleccione **Add Source** y elija el Source con **Select Existing** o **Add New**.
   - Mediante Routes: seleccione **Data > Sources**, después **Add Source** y **Trellix**.
2. En **New Source**, configure **General Settings**:
   - **Input ID**: nombre único para identificar esta definición. Al clonarla, Cribl añade `-CLONE` al Input ID original.
   - **Description**: descripción del Source.
   - **Address**: hostname o dirección IP para recibir HTTP/HTTPS. El valor predeterminado es `0.0.0.0`; admite IPv4 e IPv6.
   - **Port**: puerto de escucha del Source.
   - **HEC endpoint**: conserve `/services/collector`. Cribl deriva de esta ruta los endpoints de eventos y salud.
3. En **Optional Settings**:
   - **Allowed indexes**: valores permitidos en el campo HEC `index`. Admite comodines; déjelo vacío para omitir la validación. Estos valores pueden ampliar la validación de índices a nivel del token.
   - **Tags**: etiquetas para filtrar y agrupar Sources; no se añaden a los eventos procesados.
4. Ajuste **TLS**, **Persistent Queue**, **Processing**, **Auth Tokens**, **Advanced** y **Connected Destinations** si es necesario. Consulte la página completa para todas las opciones y restricciones de despliegue.
5. Seleccione **Save** y **Commit & Deploy**.

## TLS del servidor

**Enabled** activa TLS; está desactivado de forma predeterminada. Si lo activa, configure el certificado del servidor.

- **Certificate**: seleccione un certificado existente o use **Create** para añadir uno.
- **Certificate path**: ruta de los certificados PEM; admite `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Private key path**: ruta de la clave privada PEM; admite `$ENV_VARS`.
- **Passphrase**: contraseña para descifrar la clave privada.

Para mTLS, active **Authenticate client (mutual auth)** si es necesario. Configure **Trusted client CA path** y **Validate client certificates**, que está activado de forma predeterminada. En **Common name**, defina la expresión regular para CN y SAN del certificado del cliente; el valor predeterminado es `/.*/`.

Use **Minimum TLS version** y **Maximum TLS version** para limitar las versiones aceptadas.

## Auth Tokens

Añada uno o más tokens para autenticar Trellix NDR. **Sin un token configurado, el Source permite acceso sin autenticación.**

Seleccione **Add Token** y configure:

- **Authentication method**: elija **Secret**. Este Source no admite tokens introducidos manualmente.
- **Token secret (text secret)**: elija **Select local secret** o **Select global secret**, seleccione un secreto de texto existente o use **Create text secret**.
- **Enable token**: permite acceso con el token; está activado de forma predeterminada.
- **Description**: descripción utilizada como nombre del token.
- **Allowed indexes**: valores permitidos en el campo HEC `index` para este token; admite comodines. Déjelo vacío para omitir la validación.
- **Fields**: use **Add Field** para añadir pares **Field Name** y **Value** a los eventos que utilizan el token.

## Configurar Trellix NDR para enviar datos

Después de guardar el Source, añada una integración Splunk en Trellix NDR siguiendo [Configure SIEM using Web UI](https://docs.trellix.com/bundle/ndr_4.x_console_pg/page/UUID-2103cb9d-568f-5d93-a2db-aca0f55d47cc.html).

- **IP address or hostname**: dirección que Trellix NDR utiliza para alcanzar el Source.
- **Port**: puerto configurado en el Source.
- **Authentication**: valor del secreto de texto indicado en **Auth Tokens**.
- **SSL**: actívelo si ha activado TLS en el Source.
- **Notification**: actívelo para enviar alertas, metadatos de capa 7 y eventos de flujo.

## Endpoints HEC

Conserve **HEC endpoint** como `/services/collector`. Trellix NDR envía eventos estructurados a `/services/collector/event`. El Source admite comprobaciones de salud en `/services/collector/health`.

Las solicitudes a `/services/collector/raw` devuelven HTTP `404`. Las solicitudes a `/services/collector/ack` devuelven HTTP `400` con `ACK is disabled`.

Esta es una traducción revisada de las secciones de configuración. Las opciones detalladas de persistent queues, procesamiento, configuración avanzada y troubleshooting están en la [página oficial completa](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-trellix/).
